channel.title: Paksh: Society
channel.description: Paksh maps how India's media covers every story — coverage, gaps, and how it develops, in English and Hindi.

item.title: Meghan Markle's public appearances described as 'rare'
item.description: Meghan Markle's public appearances, described as 'royal-style visits', are expected to be 'relatively rare' and 'few and far between'. Reports indicate this is because she is currently reading a lot of scripts. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 0 · Right 1.

item.title: Louvre Director Warns of Closure Risk Without Major Overhaul
item.description: The director of the Louvre Museum has warned that the institution could be forced to close if it does not undergo a major overhaul. The museum needs to be repaired, updated, and transformed to avoid this risk. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Durga Idols Adorned with Gold and Size Draw Attention
item.description: A Durga idol in Siliguri is adorned with 100 kg of gold ornaments. Meanwhile, in Hyderabad, an 81-foot Durga idol has become a notable attraction during Navratri celebrations. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: Ambedkar University Suspends 10 Students After Campus Clashes
item.description: Dr B R Ambedkar University has suspended 10 students following clashes that occurred during a protest and documentary screening. The university has barred the suspended students from entering its campuses while a disciplinary inquiry is… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: ICAI CA Intermediate Exam Results Expected October 22
item.description: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) is expected to release the results for the CA Intermediate September 2026 examinations around October 22, 2026. The exams were held between September 1 and September 12, 2026. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: APJ Abdul Kalam's Life-Altering Question and Journey
item.description: A question about how birds fly profoundly impacted the life of APJ Abdul Kalam. His journey from selling newspapers to becoming President of India is highlighted, detailing his struggles, dedication, scientific career, and rise to the… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Jammu and Kashmir Schools Adjust Timings Due to Cold Weather
item.description: Schools in Jammu and Kashmir have changed their timings to accommodate the cold weather. Classes outside the Srinagar municipal limits will now commence at 10:30 am and conclude at 4:00 pm. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Albania Student Protests Turn Violent in Tirana
item.description: Student protests in Albania's capital, Tirana, escalated into violence on the second day of demonstrations. Riot police were deployed in response to the clashes. The protests are referred to as the 'Flamingo Revolution'. Coverage: Left 2 · Centre 7 · Right 0.

item.title: Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 Winners Announced
item.description: The winners of the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 competition have been announced, featuring striking images. Among the winning entries are photographs of an urban coyote and an elephant carrying a dead calf. A total of 19 winning… Coverage: Left 2 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: World's Oldest Shipwreck Discovered Off Turkish Coast
item.description: Divers have discovered what is believed to be the world's oldest shipwreck off the coast of Turkey. The wreck is estimated to be up to 4,700 years old, dating back to the Early Bronze Age. Coverage: Left 3 · Centre 5 · Right 0.

item.title: Boat Capsizes in Bihar's Ganga River, Killing at Least 13 Children
item.description: At least 13 children died when a boat capsized in the Ganga River in Bihar's Vaishali district. Rescue teams searched the river for missing passengers. One report stated 14 people, including women and children, were killed. The boat was… Coverage: Left 3 · Centre 4 · Right 1.

item.title: Winnie-the-Pooh Celebrates 100th Birthday
item.description: Winnie-the-Pooh, the beloved children's book character created by A.A. Milne, is celebrating his 100th birthday. The occasion has prompted discussions, including a report that Britain is seeking the return of the bear. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Kanya Pujan 2026 Dates and Rituals Discussed
item.description: Coverage from Indian outlets discusses the observance of Kanya Pujan in 2026, focusing on the appropriate dates and rituals. Questions arise regarding whether the puja should be performed on Durga Ashtami or Mahanavami, with references… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 3.

item.title: Lotto Max Jackpot Reaches Historic $90 Million
item.description: The Lotto Max lottery prize has reached $90 million, making it the largest prize in Canadian history. The jackpot has grown to this historic amount. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 3 · Right 0.

item.title: Bake Off Contestant Departs to Be With Mother in Final Days
item.description: Nikki, a contestant on The Great British Bake Off, has left the competition to be with her mother during her final days. The show and fellow contestants have paid tribute to her decision. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: New York City to Ban Horse-Drawn Carriages After Tourist's Death
item.description: New York City has agreed to ban horse-drawn carriages, a decision that follows the death of 18-year-old Indian tourist Romanch Mahajan. Mahajan died on June 17 from injuries sustained in an accident in Central Park where he fell from a… Coverage: Left 5 · Centre 7 · Right 1.

item.title: France Sees Widespread School Protests, Greta Thunberg Joins
item.description: Tens of thousands of people, including schoolchildren, students, and trade unionists, participated in protests across France for the third consecutive week. On Tuesday, between 161,500 and 480,000 people marched, with Swedish activist… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 5 · Right 2.

item.title: Bald Eagle Jackie's Cause of Death Revealed
item.description: Jackie, a bald eagle known for its presence at the National Eagle Center in Wabasha, Minnesota, has died. The cause of death has been revealed, and the bird has been cremated. Jackie was a notable figure at the center. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: Boat Capsizes in Bihar's Ganga River, 14 Children Dead
item.description: A boat carrying children capsized in the Ganga River in Bihar's Vaishali district, resulting in the deaths of 14 children. The children were reportedly on their way to attend a 'shraddh bhoj' (a ritual meal) at a relative's house. The… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: PM Modi Highlights Global Recognition of India's Cultural Heritage
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that India's cultural heritage is gaining increasing recognition internationally. This statement was made in coverage from both centrist and right-leaning outlets. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: Ektaa Kapoor Alleges Hinduphobia in Bollywood Over Religious Symbols
item.description: Producer Ektaa Kapoor has stated that Bollywood exhibits "Hinduphobia," citing instances where wearing religious symbols like a 'tika' is perceived as problematic. She specifically mentioned this as an issue within the film industry. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: Visa Rejection and Travel Insurance Coverage
item.description: A visa application fee was paid, but the visa was subsequently rejected. The coverage raises the question of whether travel insurance can assist in such situations, specifically detailing the concept of 'fraudulent payment card cover'… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 0 · Right 1.

item.title: Students Protest, Demand Vice-Chancellor's Resignation Over Campus Violence
item.description: Students at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) have begun an indefinite sit-in protest, demanding the resignation of the Vice-Chancellor. The protest follows reported campus violence. Coverage: Left 2 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Mauritius Imposes Curfew Amid Worst Riots in Decades
item.description: Mauritius imposed a curfew following days of unrest described as the worst riots in decades, which began over water shortages and escalated after a woman was shot by police. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam announced the curfew. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Padma Shri awardee Cheruvayal Raman, preserver of traditional rice, dies
item.description: Cheruvayal Raman, a Padma Shri awardee known for preserving 45 traditional rice varieties, has died. He was 74 or 75 years old. Raman was recognized as a guardian of Wayanad's traditional paddy seeds. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 3 · Right 0.

item.title: Taliban Suspends BBC FM Radio Broadcasts in Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban has suspended BBC FM radio broadcasts across Afghanistan, citing "repeated violations." The BBC stated it is working to resolve the dispute with the authorities. BBC programming remains accessible to audiences via shortwave… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Prince William Plays Cricket in London, Earthshot Prize to Visit India
item.description: Prince William participated in a game of cricket outside Buckingham Palace in London. He was described as a "pretty good" batsman by Joe Root. The Earthshot Prize, an initiative led by Prince William, is set to be held in India. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 1.

item.title: Author Denies Using AI for Award-Winning Story Amid Plagiarism Claims
item.description: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied accusations of using artificial intelligence to write his award-winning story, which has caused an uproar on social media. Separately, a Quebec author admitted to past plagiarism but denied… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 3 · Right 1.

item.title: Irish Public Sector Workers Strike Over Pay Dispute
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of public sector workers in the Republic of Ireland went on strike due to an ongoing pay dispute with the government. The strike led to school closures and the cancellation of medical appointments. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 4 · Right 0.

item.title: Farmers Block Highways Demanding Higher Sugar Prices and Better Procurement
item.description: Farmers have blocked the Pune-Bengaluru national highway near Belagavi for a second consecutive day, causing traffic disruptions. The protest, involving sugarcane farmers, is centered on demands for a higher Minimum Support Price (MSP) for… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 4 · Right 1.

item.title: Michelin Guide Awards First Australian Stars to South Australian Restaurants
item.description: The Michelin Guide has awarded its first-ever stars to 11 restaurants in Australia, all located in South Australia. Reports suggest the state government funded visits by incognito inspectors, which may have influenced the selection. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: London's Oldest Restaurant Site Donated to National Trust
item.description: The property housing Rules, London's oldest restaurant, has been gifted to the National Trust. The site is valued at £11 million. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: Black music events face barriers, investigation finds
item.description: An investigation into London's live music industry has found that Black and South Asian music events face disproportionate cancellations, restrictions, and licensing barriers compared to white-led events. The study suggests these… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: Charlotte Church Closes Wellness Retreat
item.description: Singer Charlotte Church has been compelled to close her wellness retreat. The retreat featured a 'womb room'. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: Van Gogh Painting Surfaces in Hong Kong Ahead of Auction
item.description: A rarely seen landscape painting by Vincent van Gogh, titled "Châtaigniers en fleurs" (Chestnut Trees in Blossom), has been unveiled in Hong Kong. The painting is on display ahead of its auction in New York this weekend, where it is… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Maharashtra to launch air ambulance service on accident-prone highways
item.description: Maharashtra plans to introduce an air ambulance service along three major highways that experience the highest number of accidents. Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik announced that the service will operate on the Nagpur-Mumbai Samruddhi… Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 1 · Right 1.

item.title: Indian-Australian Author Siya Jain Launches Second Book at UK Parliament
item.description: Indian-Australian author Siya Jain launched her second book at the UK Parliament. She also received a Certificate of Excellence during the event. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 1 · Right 0.

item.title: Maharashtra declares 85% areas drought-hit, announces farmer aid
item.description: Maharashtra has declared 85 percent of its areas as drought-hit, adding 40 talukas to the drought list. The state government announced that farmers in these regions will receive ₹5,000 each as aid before Diwali. The opposition has… Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 0.

item.title: Influencer's Diwali Sweet Request Leads to Fake COD Orders
item.description: An Indian influencer's request for Diwali sweets, shared online with his address, resulted in him receiving fake Cash on Delivery (COD) orders for a ₹1.69 lakh television. The incident, described as a nightmare ordeal, went viral. Coverage: Left 0 · Centre 2 · Right 1.

item.title: NCC Founder A.V.S. Raju, Padma Shri Recipient, Dies at 89
item.description: A.V.S. Raju, the founder of NCC Ltd and a Padma Shri awardee, has passed away at the age of 89. Raju was recognized as a lifelong builder of NCC and a pioneer in Andhra business. He died in Hyderabad. Coverage: Left 1 · Centre 2 · Right 0.
